slider.title: EVIDENCE THRESHOLD
slider.treatment: Treat this evidence threshold as a hard calibration for every claim.

items.label: Minimum support
items.frame: Prefer claims supported by multiple primary lines; label anything weaker explicitly.

dial.title: ANCESTOR LANGUAGE
dial.treatment: Calibrate how literally the answer may describe fossils as ancestors.

items.label: Direct-ancestor caution
items.frame: Treat named fossils as side relatives unless direct ancestry is specifically demonstrated.

count.title: PRIMARY SOURCES
count.treatment: Meet the requested source count without inventing citations.

items.label: Minimum primary DOI links
items.frame: Name at least this many relevant primary papers already present in the connected evidence.

switch.title: SHOW LIVE ALTERNATIVES
switch.treatment: Keep unresolved branches visible instead of averaging them away.

items.label: State incompatible hypotheses
items.frame: Show each supported alternative completely and say what evidence would discriminate between them.

items.label: Preserve invariant conclusions
items.frame: Separate conclusions that survive every live alternative from those that change.

pad.title: SCOPE × CAUTION
pad.treatment: Balance breadth against evidential caution using both axes together.

x.label: Scope
x.frame: Move from a local datum toward its consequences for the whole chicken-history model.

y.label: Caution
y.frame: Raise the burden of identity, date type, sampling, and directionality before asserting a conclusion.

select.title: ANSWER SHAPE
select.treatment: Use the selected structure for the final synthesis.

options.label: Narrative
options.frame: Write a chronological narrative with explicit caveats.

options.label: Claim–evidence–caveat–test
options.frame: For each conclusion give the claim, best evidence, strongest caveat, and deciding next test.

options.label: Decision table
options.frame: Compare alternatives in a compact decision table.

order.title: SYNTHESIS PRIORITY
order.treatment: Respect this ordering when allocating attention and words.

items.label: Stable topology
items.frame: Begin with the nesting that is robust across analyses.

items.label: Network and domestication
items.frame: Then explain gene flow and the difference between source ancestry and a human event.

items.label: Uncertainty and next tests
items.frame: Finish with live alternatives and the cheapest decisive observations.

state.frame: Do not let a disputed oldest-known claim displace the stable evolutionary scaffold.

filter.title: CLAIM ADMISSION
filter.treatment: Filter claims by identity, dating, and directionality before they enter the synthesis.

lanes.label: Taxon or specimen identity
lanes.frame: Require comparative morphology, CT, ZooMS, DNA, or a clearly stated combined method.

lanes.label: Chronology
lanes.frame: Name whether the date is a fossil occurrence, clock, demographic split, associated phase, or direct AMS.

lanes.label: Arrow direction
lanes.frame: Draw a directional introgression arrow only when donor and recipient direction are supported.

mixer.title: EVIDENCE MIX
mixer.treatment: Blend disciplines in these proportions without treating unlike date types as interchangeable.

state.frame: Triangulate rather than averaging incompatible measurements.

items.label: Phylogenomics and fossils
items.frame: Use topology, character combinations, stratigraphy, and clock sensitivity.

items.label: Population genomics
items.frame: Use sampling, demographic models, local ancestry, and direction caveats.

items.label: Archaeology and biomolecules
items.frame: Use context, direct dates, ZooMS, isotopes, age profiles, and depositional evidence.

radar.title: AUDIT COVERAGE
radar.treatment: Make weak audit dimensions visible rather than hiding them in fluent prose.

axes.label: Primary-source traceability
axes.frame: Tie every material claim to a connected primary source.

axes.label: Alternative hypotheses
axes.frame: Represent each live topology or interpretation completely.

axes.label: Sampling limitations
axes.frame: Name geography, sample type, captive status, preservation, and missing reference panels.

axes.label: Decisive tests
axes.frame: End each uncertainty with the observation most likely to change the conclusion.

matrix.title: CLAIM × EVIDENCE STATUS
matrix.treatment: Use the matrix to distinguish what is observed, modeled, and unresolved.
